title: This Insect Looks Like a Flower and Beats Real Flowers at Their Own Job
subject: orchid mantis

scenes.text: This insect isn't a flower. Bees fly to it more than to real ones.
It's the orchid mantis, pink and white, with legs shaped like petals.
Researchers put mantises out in the field. Pollinators came to them about thirty percent more often than to real flowers.
The bees don't land to feed. They land on a predator that is sitting perfectly still.
Then the mantis snaps its front legs shut and catches the visitor.
Scientists call it the first animal shown to hunt by posing as a flower.

description:
A mantis that looks like an orchid attracted pollinators at a higher rate than real flowers.
The visitors it attracts become its prey.
Which animal fools its prey best?
first_comment: Would you land on a flower if it looked perfect? Which animal's disguise is the best you know?
